notes.md: - **Indira Prabha and Indira Jala Prabha:** **Indira Prabha (2007)** – AP scheme to develop lands assigned to the poor and bring them under cultivation. **Indira Jala Prabha (October 2011)** – irrigation (borewells) on SC and ST farmers' lands, funded by **NABARD under RIDF-XVII** (about ₹399 crore) with **MGNREGS**.
- **National Kamdhenu Breeding Centres (Rashtriya Gokul Mission):** stores of elite **indigenous germplasm**; southern centre at **Chintaladevi, Nellore (AP)**, northern centre at **Itarsi (MP)**.

new.s: Agricultural loans up to how many months are classed as short-term credit?
new.x: Short-term farm credit runs up to 15 months; medium-term is 15 months to 5 years.
new.angle: U0499 notes gap: short-term credit up to 15 months

new.s: What are Land Development Banks now called?
o: Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Banks
new.x: Land Development Banks, the long-term arm of the cooperative structure, are now called Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Banks.
new.angle: U0499 notes gap: LDBs renamed CARDBs

new.s: How many Regional Rural Banks were set up in 1975?
new.x: Five RRBs were set up in 1975, the first being Prathama Grameen Bank at Moradabad.
new.angle: U0499 notes gap: 5 RRBs in 1975

new.s: On which date was NABARD established?
new.x: NABARD was set up on 12 July 1982 under the NABARD Act, 1981.
new.angle: U0499 notes gap: NABARD established 12 July 1982

new.s:
Consider the following statements about NABARD:
1. It was established on 12 July 1982.
2. It was established during the Fifth Five Year Plan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: NABARD was set up on 12 July 1982, during the Sixth Five Year Plan, not the Fifth.
new.angle: U0499 notes gap: NABARD establishment date

new.s: In which year did NABARD set up the ₹2,000 crore Food Processing Fund?
new.x: The Food Processing Fund of ₹2,000 crore came in 2014-15; the Warehouse Infrastructure Fund came in 2013-14.
new.angle: U0499 notes gap: NABARD Food Processing Fund

new.s: On whose Working Group's recommendation were electronic Kisan Credit Cards introduced?
new.x: Electronic KCCs follow the T.M. Bhasin Working Group; R.V. Gupta recommended the KCC itself.
new.angle: U0499 notes gap: e-KCC T.M. Bhasin Working Group

new.s: About how many Kisan Credit Cards were operative as on 31 March 2025?
new.x: There were 7.72 crore operative KCCs on 31 March 2025, with ₹10.20 lakh crore outstanding.
new.angle: U0499 notes gap: operative KCCs data

new.s: What type of scheme is the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS)?
new.x: MISS is a Central Sector scheme run through RBI and NABARD.
new.angle: U0499 notes gap: MISS a Central Sector scheme

new.s: What is the priority sector lending target for non-corporate farmers?
new.x: Non-corporate farmers have a 14% target, within the 18% agriculture target; small and marginal farmers have 10%.
new.angle: U0499 notes gap: PSL non-corporate farmers 14%

new.s: Which region of India gets about 48 per cent of agricultural credit with only about 17 per cent of the cropped area?
new.x: Agricultural credit is skewed to the South (48%); the East gets only 8.2% and the Central region 13.7%.
new.angle: U0499 notes gap: regional skew of agri credit

new.s: Under which NABARD fund was Andhra Pradesh's Indira Jala Prabha (2011) financed?
new.x: NABARD sanctioned about ₹399 crore for Indira Jala Prabha under RIDF-XVII, in convergence with MGNREGS.
new.angle: U0499 web: PYQ y0fab4f31f90 AP programme with NABARD support

new.s: What did Indira Jala Prabha, launched in Andhra Pradesh in 2011, mainly provide on the lands of SC and ST farmers?
new.x: Indira Jala Prabha gave irrigation (borewells) on SC and ST farmers' lands with NABARD RIDF and MGNREGS funds.
new.angle: U0499 web: PYQ y0fab4f31f90 AP programme with NABARD support

new.s: About how many regulated agricultural markets are there in India?
new.x: India has about 2,477 regulated markets and 4,843 sub-yards.
new.angle: U0500 notes gap: number of regulated markets

new.s: Which slogan is associated with e-NAM?
new.x: e-NAM, launched in April 2016, works on the idea of 'One Nation, One Market'.
new.angle: U0500 notes gap: e-NAM slogan

new.s: Up to how much assistance is given per mandi for joining e-NAM?
new.x: Each mandi joining e-NAM can get up to ₹75 lakh.
new.angle: U0500 notes gap: e-NAM support per mandi

new.s: About how many Rythu Bazars were functional in Andhra Pradesh in 2025-26?
new.x: Andhra Pradesh had 129 functional Rythu Bazars in 2025-26.
new.angle: U0500 notes gap: AP Rythu Bazars count

new.s: What is the size of the Agri-Market Infrastructure Fund set up for Gramin Agricultural Markets (GrAMs)?
new.x: A ₹2,000 crore Agri-Market Infrastructure Fund supports the upgrading of rural haats into GrAMs.
new.angle: U0500 notes gap: GrAMs Agri-Market Infrastructure Fund

new.s: In which year was TRIFED set up?
new.x: TRIFED, for marketing tribal produce, was set up in 1987; NAFED dates from 1958.
new.angle: U0500 notes gap: TRIFED year

new.s: In which year was the Warehousing Development and Regulatory Authority (WDRA) set up?
new.x: WDRA was set up on 26 October 2010; the Act was passed in 2007.
new.angle: U0500 notes gap: WDRA year

new.s: Through which body is credit guarantee given for loans under the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund?
new.x: AIF loans up to ₹2 crore get credit guarantee through CGTMSE.
new.angle: U0500 notes gap: AIF credit guarantee via CGTMSE

new.s: How many oilseeds are covered under Minimum Support Price?
new.x: Seven oilseeds have MSP: groundnut, rapeseed-mustard, soybean, sunflower, sesamum, safflower and nigerseed.
new.angle: U0501 notes gap: oilseeds under MSP

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a pillar of the WTO Agreement on Agriculture?
new.x: The three pillars of the Agreement on Agriculture are market access, domestic support and export subsidies.
new.angle: U0501 notes gap: WTO AoA pillars

new.s: Under the WTO Agreement on Agriculture, which box covers production-limiting payments?
new.x: Blue box covers production-limiting payments; green box covers research and infrastructure; amber box covers trade-distorting support.
new.angle: U0501 notes gap: WTO blue box

new.s: From which date has free foodgrain been given under PMGKAY to over 80 crore NFSA beneficiaries?
new.x: Free grain under PMGKAY began on 1 January 2023 and is extended to 31 December 2028.
new.angle: U0502 notes gap: PMGKAY free grain start date

new.s: How many States and UTs does One Nation One Ration Card now cover?
new.x: ONORC now runs in all 36 States/UTs, covering about 80 crore beneficiaries.
new.angle: U0502 notes gap: ONORC coverage

new.s: As per APSES 2024-25, about how many people benefit from the PDS in Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: AP's PDS has about 1.48 crore beneficiaries served through 29,796 Fair Price Shops.
new.angle: U0502 notes gap: AP PDS beneficiaries

new.s: Which State has the highest share of stunted children as per the Poshan Tracker (July 2025)?
new.x: Uttar Pradesh leads in stunting (48.8%); Bihar leads in wasting and Madhya Pradesh in underweight.
new.angle: U0503 notes gap: highest stunting State

new.s: In which year was the National Nutritional Anaemia Prophylaxis Programme launched?
new.x: The National Nutritional Anaemia Prophylaxis Programme began in 1970; Anaemia Mukt Bharat came in 2018.
new.angle: U0503 notes gap: NNAPP 1970

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a pillar of POSHAN Abhiyaan?
new.x: POSHAN Abhiyaan seeks Suposhit Bharat through convergence, technology and Jan Andolan.
new.angle: U0503 notes gap: POSHAN Abhiyaan pillars

new.s: Which schemes were covered in Phase I (2021-22) of fortified rice distribution?
new.x: Phase I covered ICDS and PM POSHAN; Phase II covered 291 districts and Phase III all TPDS districts.
new.angle: U0503 notes gap: fortification Phase I

new.s: With which products is the Pink Revolution associated?
new.x: The Pink Revolution relates to meat and poultry (also onion); eggs are the Silver Revolution.
new.angle: U0504 notes gap: Pink Revolution

new.s: In which year was the National Livestock Mission launched?
new.x: The National Livestock Mission began in 2014-15 and was revised in 2021-22.
new.angle: U0504 notes gap: NLM launch

new.s: Under which scheme were the National Kamdhenu Breeding Centres at Chintaladevi and Itarsi set up?
new.x: The National Kamdhenu Breeding Centres were set up under the Rashtriya Gokul Mission as stores of indigenous germplasm.
new.angle: U0504 web: PYQ y73000f443f9 Chintaladeevi centre

new.s: Where is the National Kamdhenu Breeding Centre for southern India located?
new.x: The southern National Kamdhenu Breeding Centre is at Chintaladevi in Nellore district; the northern one is at Itarsi.
new.angle: U0504 web: PYQ y73000f443f9 Chintaladeevi centre

new.s: How many indigenous breeds were covered in the 21st Livestock Census?
new.x: The 21st Livestock Census (Oct 2024 - Feb 2025) covered 16 species and 219 indigenous breeds.
new.angle: U0504 notes gap: 21st Livestock Census breeds

new.s: What is India's rank in world meat production?
new.x: India is 4th in meat (10.50 MT); West Bengal is the leading State.
new.angle: U0504 notes gap: India rank in meat

new.s: In which year was Operation Flood launched?
new.x: Operation Flood ran from 1970 to 1996 in three phases; NDDB was set up in 1965.
new.angle: U0504 notes gap: Operation Flood launch year

new.s: Which country is the largest producer of fish in the world?
new.x: China is the largest fish producer (36% in 2022, SOFIA 2024); India is second.
new.angle: U0504 notes gap: largest fish producer China

new.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. China produced about 36 per cent of the world's fish in 2022.
2. India is the second largest fish producer with about 8 per cent of world output.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: SOFIA 2024 puts China at 36%; India is second with about 8%.
